name: encryption-bitwarden
title: Encryption key sources — env (default, kept) + Bitwarden Secrets Manager via bws CLI

ownerGateReview.form: owner rulings f: 2026-08-05 (docs/work/archive/2026-08-05-db-passphrase-options.md 'Owner decisions' section, superseding report F28)
ownerGateReview.note: All decisions ruled inline by the owner during the 2026-08-05 research follow-ups: env kept, bws CLI (not SDK), SSH-key secret value with measured derivation, refuse-to-start offline, rotation warning, raw-key file removed.

cards.ruling: AIRACCOON_DB_PASSPHRASE STAYS as the default key source (zero-setup path; the single-channel ruling's documented exception).
bws CLI, not the SDK: provider shells out to 'bws secret get <id>' at bank open; SDK caveats (beta, sync API, custom license, 7MB native binary) are moot.

The secret's VALUE is an unencrypted ed25519 SSH private key; derived with SHA-256("ai-raccoon-db-key/v1" || seed) -> x'<64hex>' raw SQLCipher key (no KDF, measured). RSA and passphrase-protected keys rejected.
Refuse to start, loudly; no cached key copy.
Rotating the secret in the Bitwarden UI without PRAGMA rekey bricks the bank — the config command warns.

encryption bitwarden: (a) bws presence check with install guidance error; (b) collect project id + secret id (defaults from AIRACCOON_BITWARDEN_PROJECT_ID / AIRACCOON_BITWARDEN_SECRET_ID; absent those, an obviously-fake placeholder id); (c) optional -t <token> for runs without BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN — passed for that run only, never persisted.
REMOVED. Provider family = env + bitwarden; keychain/cloud stay documented future sources.
Inferred (flag at gate): encryption show prints the current source; encryption unset returns to the env default.

IEncryptionKeyProvider becomes a source-selectable family; selection persisted in the settings table (encryption.source, encryption.bitwarden.projectId, encryption.bitwarden.secretId) — settings rows are read pre-open from the bank header path only where safe; the source SELECTION lives outside the encrypted content (settings table is inside the bank — the selection is read AFTER open from settings; the env path is the pre-open bootstrap, bitwarden selection must be resolvable pre-open, so the source selection is stored in a small unencrypted sidecar or derived from bank presence — implementation decision flagged).

in: IEncryptionKeyProvider source family: env (default, kept) + bitwarden (bws CLI)

BitwardenEncryptionKeyProvider: runs 'bws secret get <secret-id>' (optionally with -t token), parses the ed25519 private key, derives SHA-256("ai-raccoon-db-key/v1" || seed) -> x'<64hex>', returns it through the existing Password channel
Reject RSA and passphrase-protected (encrypted) private keys with clear errors

ai-raccoon encryption bitwarden: bws presence check (actionable install/token error when missing), interactive collection of project id + secret id (owner defaults), optional -t <token> never persisted, reachability validation, rotation-trap warning
ai-raccoon encryption show: prints the current source + bitwarden secret id when active
ai-raccoon encryption unset: returns to the env default
Refuse to start when the bitwarden source cannot produce a key (missing bws, network failure, bad secret) — loud, actionable error
Env path unchanged: AIRACCOON_DB_PASSPHRASE continues to work as today
out: Bitwarden SDK package (Bitwarden.Secrets.Sdk) — bws CLI only
Keychain / SSH-key-direct / Azure KV / AWS SM providers (documented future sources, not implemented)
Token persistence of any kind (the -t token is per-run only; BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN stays the user's own env config)

nonFunctional: No new NuGet package for Bitwarden — the bws binary is the integration surface
Secrets never on argv beyond the user's own -t flag, and never persisted by ai-raccoon
Refuse-to-start semantics: the bank cannot open without the configured source's key; failures are loud and actionable
Clean layering: derivation (pure crypto from the SSH key seed) in Core; bws process invocation in Infrastructure; config command in the CLI layer
TDD mandatory: scenario + unit tests for derivation (deterministic, wrong-key rejection), provider errors, config flow
TreatWarningsAsErrors; dotnet build + dotnet test green

targets.tests: tests/AiRaccoon.Tests (derivation unit tests, provider tests with a fake bws, config command tests)

risks: The source SELECTION must be resolvable pre-DB-open (the bank is encrypted; the settings table is inside it) — the bitwarden selection cannot live only in the settings table; a small unencrypted sidecar next to the bank or env override is required. Implementation must decide and pin this (D9).
Rotation trap: web-UI rotation without PRAGMA rekey bricks the bank — warning at config time is the mitigation
bws output parsing: secret value format must be validated as an OpenSSH ed25519 private key (RFC 8709) before derivation; malformed values must error clearly
Passphrase-protected keys: detection via the OpenSSH 'bcrypt' cipher field — must be rejected, not mis-derived
The measured derivation label ('ai-raccoon-db-key/v1') is a stability contract — changing it silently breaks existing banks

deferred.decision: Keychain / SSH-key-direct / Azure Key Vault / AWS Secrets Manager providers
deferred.fallback: Documented future sources behind the same IEncryptionKeyProvider interface (research: docs/work/archive/2026-08-05-db-passphrase-options.md + ssh-and-cloud-vaults.md)
